name: Pump.fun
thesis: PUMP earns far more per dollar of value than its listed peers, but dated team and investor unlocks and a falling price mean the balance of evidence tilts lower, not strongly enough for a directional view.

note.name: Pump.fun
note.thesis: PUMP earns far more per dollar of value than its listed peers, but dated team and investor unlocks and a falling price mean the balance of evidence tilts lower, not strongly enough for a directional view.
note.what: Pump.fun is a Solana memecoin launchpad. Users start a coin at no cost, trade it on a bonding curve, and pay to graduate it to PumpSwap, the platform's own exchange. The PUMP token is not needed to use the platform and carries no claim on revenue.

points.text: Thirty-day fees of $138.45M annualise to $1.68B; the last seven days annualise to $1.27B. All-time fees are $2.41B.
Half of platform revenue buys PUMP in the open market and burns it permanently; 176.41B PUMP has been burned for $505.18M.
Team and existing-investor wallets sent 76,111 SOL ($6.85M) to Kraken, Lookonchain reported, part of a running series of transfers.
PUMP is $0.00353227, down 31.8% over 30 days and 16.0% over seven, sitting at its 30-day low of $0.00350.
PUMP trades at 1.7x annualised fees against a 5.4x peer median, and 4.8x annualised revenue against 13.1x.
points.source: DefiLlama and CoinGecko peer read, 11 Nov 2026

note.supplyHeadline: Unlocks go to team and investors
note.supplyText: Over the next 90 days 20.625B PUMP is released to the team and existing investors, starting on 12 November 2026, equal to 4.5% of circulating supply. Two cliffs of 6.875B fall on 11 December 2026 and 11 January 2027. Only the documented schedule is counted; other inflation may exist.
note.valuationText: Revenue, not gross fees, funds the buyback, so revenue is the measure that matters here. The peer group is wide: revenue multiples run from 1.5x (Graphite Protocol) to 57.6x (Uniswap), and the set mixes launchpads and DEXs, each measured on its whole business.
note.usageText: PumpSwap supplies 60% of fees but only 21% of revenue; the launchpad supplies 36% of fees and 71% of revenue. The recent cooling in the fee pace has no identified cause.

catalysts.text: First new tokens of the 90-day vesting schedule reach the market.
6.875B cliff, about $24.53M at the 11 November price, to team and investors.
Second 6.875B cliff on the same schedule.

risks.title: Buybacks accelerate
risks.text: A step-up in burn spending would absorb unlock supply and undercut the lower tilt.

risks.title: Price reclaims 30-day high
risks.text: A close above $0.00513, the 22 October high, would break the downtrend the tilt rests on.

risks.title: December unlock absorbed
risks.text: If the 11 December cliff passes without fresh insider exchange deposits, the supply concern weakens.

risks.title: Fee slowdown steepens
risks.text: Seven-day annualised fees falling further below the 30-day pace would argue for a directional bearish view, not neutral.

watchlist.item: Sparsity: about three-quarters of revenue from tokens listed under an hour
Cumulative insider SOL: 5,553,833 SOL versus 5.627M SOL
Points or emissions programme and its size

note.positioningText: Funding is +0.0100%/8h now and has averaged +0.0051%/8h over seven days. Open interest across exchanges is $57M, down 15.3% over that week. The long/short account ratio is 0.74, with 42% of accounts long.
note.conclusion: The burn is verifiable and the platform is priced well below comparable venues; the scheduled insider supply and the price trend argue the other way. Positioning is not crowded either way, so the 11 December cliff and the pace of buybacks will settle which force wins.
note.invalidation: 7-day annualised fees back above the 30-day pace for two weeks running.
note.gaps: No verified points or emissions programme, so total future issuance may be understated. Fee totals disagree: Grip Research's $176.91M against DefiLlama's $138.45M. Circulating supply also conflicts, with Codex Scan showing 354B against CoinGecko's 458.429B.

sources.title: pump.fun — PUMP token
sources.claim: buyback and burn funded by revenue

note.verdictHow: the research tilts lower; independent reads did not confirm it
